correctness.rationale: Compact-group Fourier-Bochner expansion with nonnegative summable coefficients reduces every admissible function to 128 parity weights for the fixed samples. An exact 14-sector Krawtchouk inequality gives Q >= 12/7 + (40/7)F03 + (60/7)F14 >= 12/7. The displayed multiaffine cosine polynomial has a nonnegative Fourier measure, satisfies 14 exact vertex-value conditions for global pointwise nonnegativity and reaches 12/7. An extracted standalone standard-library checker reproduced 510 finite rational assertions. The analytic argument, not finite testing, proves the infinite-dimensional statement.

originality.rationale: The September 2026 motivating manuscript proves a counterexample with one negative sign and explicitly optimizes the corresponding one-negative contrast, not the two-negative contrast here. The present all-function-class two-negative sharp 12/7 infimum, two-test-average dual certificate and extremizer are not implied by that result or by the squared-kernel Schur theorem. A close lacunary result addresses an odd-base compression rather than sharp two-negative minimization; its complete text was inaccessible and is a residual priority risk. In fact the published one-negative witness has Q = 82/35 > 2 for the present two-negative vector, so it does not itself witness the present failure.
residual_risks: An older unpublished or unindexed Walsh/Krawtchouk extremal calculation could imply the same sharp two-negative inequality.
One relevant lacunary-compression paper was accessible only as bibliographic summary; its full text could contain an unreported reduction.
Exact novelty is assessed relative to inspected materials and is not an independent priority certification.

value.rationale: The sharp two-negative/six-positive extremum is the next canonical signed direction after the one-negative witness on the same natural eight-node affine simplex. It settles a motivated exact spectral invariant over an infinite-dimensional cone, exhibits a larger quantitative violation (-2/7 instead of -1/10, in different directions) and provides a fully explicit small dual certificate useful for examining other contrast orbits. It is not a claim of the worst possible violation over all sample sets or contrasts.
